data.title: North Shore Closes Flow-Through Share Private Placement
data.description:
NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION TO UNITED STATES NEWSWIRE SERVICES OR FOR DISSEMINATION IN THE UNITED STATES

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / North Shore Uranium Ltd. ("North Shore" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has closed its non-brokered private placement offering previously announced on November 18, 2026 (the "Offering") for gross proceeds of $1,110,930 through the issuance of 5,847,000 flow-through common shares of the Company (each, a "FT Share"). The Offering was upsized from the previously announced maximum of $1,100,000.

Each FT Share was issued at a price of $0.19 per FT Share. Each FT Share was issued as a "flow-through share" within the meaning of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the "ITA").

The Company intends to use the gross proceeds of the Offering to incur "Canadian exploration expenses" that qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" (as such terms are defined in the ITA) on the Company's uranium properties in Saskatchewan, which will be renounced to the subscribers of FT Shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The costs of the Offering will be paid from the Company's general working capital.

In connection with the Offering, the Company paid cash finder's fees of $66,655.80 and issued 350,820 non-transferable finder's warrants to certain arm's length finders. Each non-transferable finder's warrant is exercisable to acquire one common share of the Company at a price of $0.19 per share for a period of two years from the date of closing the Offering, subject to compliance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "Exchange") and applicable securities laws.

All securities issued in connection with the Offering are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 27, 2027.

The Offering remains subject to final acceptance of the Exchange.

Caution to U.S. Investors

The securities referred to in this news release have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act"), or any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold within the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons absent registration under the U.S. Securities Act and applicable state securities laws, unless an exemption from such registration is available. This news release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy, nor shall there be any sale of the securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful. "United States" and "U.S. person" have the respective meanings assigned in Regulation S under the U.S. Securities Act.

ABOUT NORTH SHORE

The nuclear power industry is undergoing increased development to meet CO₂ emission-reduction goals and the needs of new power-intensive technologies like AI. In this environment, discoveries of uranium deposits may be significant, especially in established uranium-producing jurisdictions like New Mexico and Saskatchewan. North Shore is focused on advancing exploration for uranium deposits at Rio Puerco in the Grants Uranium District of New Mexico and its Falcon and West Bear properties at the eastern margin of the Athabasca Basin in Saskatchewan. In addition, the Company continues to evaluate quality opportunities in the United States and Canada that would complement its portfolio of uranium properties.

Brooke Clements

President, Chief Executive Officer and Director

data.title: BQE Water Reports Q3 2026 Results
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - BQE Water Inc. , a leader in the treatment and management of mine impacted waters, is pleased to release its interim consolidated financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

"With GAAP revenue up 32%, net income up 33% and Adjusted EBITDA up 38% over Q3 2025, our strong third quarter results allowed us to us to substantially narrow the gap on a year-to-date basis relative to the same period in 2025. In the third quarter, we remobilized our operations team back to the Kemess Mine, successfully restarting the treatment plant and operating it on a seasonal basis. We also initiated 3-year operations support for cyanide destruction for a facility in Alaska." said David Kratochvil, President & CEO of BQE Water. "We now have 26 treatment facilities across 11 operation sites in our recurring revenue portfolio. This growing operational base is supported by a strong pipeline of projects and opportunities that we expect to build on in the quarters ahead. In addition, we have good visibility into new near-term operating opportunities that are expected to allow us to redeploy our seasonal operations teams during the winter shutdown."

FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS

  • Revenues under GAAP of $12.3 million in Q3 2026, a record high for a 3-month period, compared to $9.3 million in Q3 2025, a 32% increase.

  • Proportional Revenues of $14.5 million in Q3 2026 compared to $10.7 million in Q3 2025, a 36% increase.

  • Gross margin of $5.9 million in Q3 2026 compared to $4.7 million in Q3 2025, a 25% increase.

  • Net income of $3.7 million in Q3 2026 compared to net income of $2.8 million in Q3 2025, a 33% increase.

  • Earnings per share (basic) of $2.84 in Q3 2026 compared to $2.15 in Q3 2025, a 32% increase.

  • Adjusted EBITDA of $4.6 million in Q3 2026 compared to $3.3 million in Q3 2025, a 38% increase.

  • Working capital of $25.1 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $21.4 million at December 31, 2025, a 17% increase.

COMMENTARY AND OUTLOOK

We are pleased to have delivered strong third quarter results, with GAAP revenue up 32%, proportional revenue up 36%, net income up 33% and adjusted EBITDA up 38% over Q3 2025. In line with our previously communicated expectations, our strong third quarter results allowed us to us to substantially narrow the gap on a year-to-date basis relative to the same period in 2025.

Matching last year's Proportional Revenue on a year-to-date basis masks the strong underlying growth in our business. Recall that 2025 included a one-time revenue contract for the equipment sale, construction, design and commissioning of the Valley Tailings Facility, which was all recorded under technical services (advisory and design) revenue. Excluding the equipment sale component of $4.6 million from 2025, our year-to-date GAAP revenue increased 13% year-over-year, while our share of revenues from joint ventures in China also grew 38%. Although we are not eliminating the possibility of future equipment sales, the Company's business model is based on professional services linked to clean water production and our strategic focus is on our ability to grow our delivery of services, not equipment.

The primary driver of our growth in Q3 2026 and year-to-date has been recurring operations and short-term operations, which accounted for 81% and 77% of our Q3 2026 and year-to-date GAAP revenue, up from 67% and 59% in the comparable 2025 periods. In 2026, the Company operated a portfolio of 26 treatment facilities across 11 operation sites. On a year-to-date basis, new operations and support services contributed $4.6 million in additional revenue when compared to the same period in 2025. With respect to short-term operations, we added two facilities in 2026, while continuing temporary treatment at Eagle Mine. The Kemess treatment plant was recommissioned and operated for a few months in 2026, and, after a one-year hiatus, we also resumed operations at Minto Mine under a new arrangement with the new property owner, Selkirk Copper.

Excluding the above-noted equipment sale, our technical advisory and engineering services revenue has also grown but not to the same degree as our operations. We expect these services to increase gradually in Q4 2026 and into the first half of 2027 as our engineers currently undergoing site-based training to join our technical teams. All engineers hired in 2026 have been assigned to our operating sites for hands-on training before transitioning into technical teams in process design, field commissioning, or technology development. This approach is integral to the Company's vision of ensuring our technical staff develops practical field experience as a foundation for their professional growth.

Our year-to-date gross margin in dollar terms remained largely consistent at approximately $11.3 million (43.0%) compared to $11.6 million (41.4%) in the comparable prior period. The 33% decrease in year-to-date net income primarily reflects our continued investment in the people and systems required to support the Company's growth. In Q3 2026, our G&A expenses also included a one-time professional fee associated with the preparation and submission of SR&ED claims related to the Company's intellectual property and technology development activities in 2024, through which we generated $745,000 in non-refundable SR&ED investment tax credits that may be applied against future corporate income taxes payable. Moreover, under recently expanded federal and provincial SR&ED programs, the Company expects future qualifying claims for 2025 and beyond to generate refundable tax credits, providing a potential source of cash recoveries.

Our balance sheet remains strong, with working capital of $25.1 million at the end of Q3 2026, up $3.7 million from December 31, 2025. Our cash and cash equivalents stood at $17.6 million, down $1.3 million over this period, largely due to an increase in accounts receivable at the end of Q3 2026. In support of our future growth, we also invested $724,000 in capital assets during 2026, including mobile equipment at Britannia, leasehold improvements and laboratory equipment for the aquatic toxicology lab, as well as computer hardware and office equipment.

We continue to have long pipeline of projects and operations to build on the quarters ahead. While certain operations are seasonal and will pause over the winter, we have good visibility into new near-term operating opportunities that are expected to enable us to redeploy operation teams and continue generating operations revenue through the winter months. We also expect to commence several feasibility studies and a significant engineering design-for-construction project in the coming months, with anticipated project durations ranging from five to ten months.

Our growing pipeline provides strong visibility over the next 18 months. Our ability to execute on these opportunities will increasingly depend on expanding and successfully onboarding our technical team members. We will also continue to invest in and implement internal systems for accounting, safety management, and resource management to support a growing organization, resulting in additional near-term expenses. With mining industry activity remaining strong, we see a healthy environment for continued growth. We nevertheless remain mindful of geopolitical and market uncertainties and will maintain a disciplined approach to hiring, investment, and resource allocation to support profitable growth.

OPERATIONAL SERVICES HIGHLIGHTS

Our operational services consist of the operation or technical supervision of water treatment plants, which generate recurring revenues from three main sources: sales of recovered metals, water treatment fees and operations support fees. The Company, with our Inuit partner Nuvumiut Development, operates four water treatment plants at Raglan Mine for Glencore Canada Corporation ("Glencore"). The plants at Raglan Mine are usually shut down in the first quarter as water stored in the outdoor reservoirs is frozen. During Q3 2026, we continued treating water across all four plants for our 23rd operating season at the mine.

In 2021, we began providing operation support to two SART (sulphidization-acidification-recycling-thickening) plants at metallurgical facilities in Shandong province, China. In 2025, we commissioned the third SART plant in the same region. All three SART plants have been under our technical supervision since the start of production. During Q3 2026, our team provided ongoing technical supervision at two of the three plants as the Shandong Gold plant was shut down.

In 2022, we began operations of a treatment plant utilizing our Selen-IX™ process to remove selenium from ash pond water for WesTech Engineering ("WesTech"). In Q3 2026, our team continued on site, providing water treatment services with the Selen-IX™ circuit to manage the presence of selenium in the feed.

In 2022, we began operations of a treatment plant utilizing a combination of nanofiltration and our proprietary selenium electroreduction process for the simultaneous removal of selenium and sulphate from mine water for a base metal project in the American Southwest. In 2023, our team began operations for a second newly constructed selenium removal water treatment plant at the same site. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide onsite operations support and technical supervision at both treatment plants.

In October 2025, we completed the commissioning of a Selen-IX™ treatment plant located at the Coeur Wharf Mine in South Dakota and began providing routine operation support. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide onsite and offsite support to the selenium removal circuit to manage the presence of selenium in the feed.

In January 2026, we assumed operational responsibility for the provision of operations and maintenance services for the Britannia Mine water treatment plant for the BC government under a 20-year arrangement. This High-Density Sludge lime treatment plant neutralizes acidity and removes heavy metals, primarily copper and zinc, from the mine water collected in the legacy underground workings prior to its discharge into Howe Sound. In Q3 2026, our team continued to operate and treat water daily without interruption until August 2026 and carried out the annual shut-down maintenance in September 2026.

In February 2026, we initiated an annual operation support arrangement with an integrated lead smelter-recycling facility in Eastern Canada. Prior to this arrangement, we completed an upgrade to the existing treatment system, implemented a new sulphate removal stage to a discharge limit of less than 1,500 mg/L and provided short-term operations support for the newly upgraded facility. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide ongoing site support and technical supervision.

In May 2026, we initiated a 3-year water treatment operations contract, with our Inuit partner Nuvumiut Development, to operate five treatment systems at the Nunavik Nickel Project owned by Canadian Royalties Inc. Treatment operations typically run from May to October depending on the volume of water requiring treatment. In Q3 2026, the operations team continued to operate across all five treatment systems.

In August 2026, we initiated a 3-year operations support contract to optimize a cyanide destruction circuit for a metallurgical facility in Alaska, USA. The support is intended to achieve consistent cyanide destruction performance, reducing reagent consumption, minimizing dilution water requirements, improving operational consistency between shifts, and ensuring effective implementation of the operating strategies and control philosophy. In Q3 2026, we mobilized our support team to support the facility.

SHORT-TERM OPERATIONS SERVICES HIGHLIGHTS

In addition to long-term operations, BQE Water provides operations and technical support services on a temporary basis at several sites. Short-term operations are non-recurring in nature with contracts typically lasting less than a year. Short-term operations during Q3 2026 are summarized below.

  • Continued providing water treatment operations services for the temporary emergency treatment system at the Eagle Gold Mine in the Yukon.

  • Continued operations at the ERDC Valley Tailings facility in the Yukon, which was constructed and commissioned last year.

  • Continued providing operations services at Minto Mine in the Yukon.

  • Initiated operations at the Kemess Mine water treatment plant in BC, which was the first selenium removal plant commissioned in 2020.

  • Demobilized our team from site services at Bell Mine in BC.

TECHNICAL SERVICES HIGHLIGHTS

BQE Water's technical expertise and IP are applicable globally across broad areas of water management. Highlights of some of our technical services and technical innovation projects during Q3 2026 are summarized below.

Trusted Advisory Services (Water Management and Water Studies)

  • Continued providing water management and treatment design advisory services to an operating mine in Ontario.

  • Completed lab testing and issued a report for ammonia management to a mining operation in Saskatchewan.

  • Continued to provide water management and treatment design advisory services to the KSM project in BC.

  • Continued providing water management and treatment design advisory services to a new mine undergoing permitting in the Yukon.

  • Initiated laboratory testing and advisory services to a new project in prefeasibility stage in Argentina.

  • Continued with detailed engineering for a water treatment system using ion exchange to expand rhenium production at an existing facility in Eastern Canada.

  • Continued to provide engineering design services for a water treatment system integrated into a rare earth extraction project in Brazil.

  • Performed a study to identify options for implementing selenium removal at an operating site in Quebec.

  • Completed engineering advisory services and restarted the selenium removal plant for short-term operations for the Kemess project in BC.

  • Completed a review of water treatment proposed for a new mine undergoing permitting in Yukon on behalf of the Yukon Government.

  • Initiated a pre-feasibility study engineering design for a plant to selectively recovery cobalt and scandium from copper heap leach solution in Chile.

  • Performed a review and assessment of opportunities to improve mine water treatment systems operations at legacy mines in Greece.

  • Performed a field assessment of selenium mitigation at a mine in Europe including a plan for implementing active treatment in the next 18 months.

Cyanide Management (Destruction and Recycle)

  • Completed engineering advisory services for cyanide destruction for a project in Australia.

  • Completed SART design for a new heap leach project in Mexico.

  • Continued providing engineering advisory services for estimating cyanide emissions, designing an emissions control system for cyanide, and revising engineering design of cyanide destruction for a project in the US.

  • Continued to provide plant engineering design services requiring an end-of-pipe cyanide level below 8 ppb to a project in the US.

  • Initiated field engineering advisory services for improving cyanide destruction performance at a mine in Alaska.

  • Continued detailed engineering for SART integration into the New Britannia mill in Manitoba, Canada.

Aquatic Toxicology Services

  • Continued assessment of chronic effects on aquatic environment caused by mine effluent at a mine in Western Canada.

  • Continued investigation into the effects of ammonia on acute toxicity under site-specific conditions at a mine in Eastern Canada.

  • Continued routine effluent toxicity quality monitoring for Eagle Mine water treatment operations and investigated the root cause of algae bloom.

  • Initiated laboratory tests required to establish a site-specific performance objective limit for sulphate and total dissolved solids at a mine in BC.

About BQE Water

BQE Water is a service provider specializing in water treatment and management for metals mining, smelting and refining. We are helping to transform the way the industry thinks about water in the context of natural resource projects by offering services and expertise which enables more sustainable water management practices and improved overall project performance at reduced risks. BQE Water invests in innovation and has developed unique intellectual property through the commercialization of several new technologies at mine sites around the world for organizations including Glencore, Jiangxi Copper, Freeport-McMoRan and the US EPA. BQE Water is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada and trades on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol BQE. Visit www.bqewater.com for more information.

(22:43 GMT) *China Shenhua Energy Plans to Place 177.0M New H Shares
(22:44 GMT) *China Shenhua Energy Placing Shares for HK$38.10 Each

(23:59 GMT) China Shenhua Energy Plans $860M Fund Raise to Pare Debt

By P.R. Venkat

China Shenhua Energy plans to raise about 6.74 billion Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$860 million, through a share placement to pare debt.

The coal and power company will place 177.0 million new H shares at HK$38.10 each, it said in a filing on Friday.

The placement price represents a 7.70% discount to Thursday's closing price of HK$41.28.

About 90% of the proceeds will be used to repay onshore debt, which rose after a large acquisition earlier this year, the company said.

Borrowings reached 157.63 billion yuan at the end of June, following a 93.52 billion yuan cash payment to acquire stakes in 12 companies from its state-owned parent, China Energy Investment.

The remaining proceeds will be allocated to working capital, primarily for tax payments. The transaction is expected to close Dec. 1.

China International Capital Corp. and CLSA are acting as placing agents.

data.title: The Relentless Rise of South Florida's Megamansion King — WSJ
data.description:
By Katherine Clarke | Photography by Zak Bennett for WSJ

Palm Beach, Fla.- Todd Michael Glaser loves making bets with his friends — but not for real money. Instead, the loser gives the winner a single dollar bill inscribed with a mea culpa. "I was wrong, you were right, you are the best." That kind of thing.

"It's good to be right," says Glaser, showing off one of the bills over lunch in Palm Beach. He's been right a lot.

Few people have benefited more than Glaser, a high-end spec-home developer, from the real estate gold rush that has transformed South Florida in recent years. As money flooded in from the Northeast during Covid, then later from Silicon Valley, Glaser has lined his and his partners' pockets by building and renovating a flurry of nine-figure megamansions for the superrich in Miami Beach and Palm Beach. All the while, the 62-year-old has earned a controversial reputation as a straight-talking, relentless hustler who does whatever it takes to carve out profits, whether it's flipping contracts, nixing deals or courting the media spotlight.

"If he could make money from the shirt on his back, he would sell the shirt on his back," says Glaser's sometime real-estate agent Nelson Gonzalez. "He would sell the shirt off your back."

Now, Glaser is making his biggest wager yet. He's building a mansion on Miami Beach's coveted North Bay Road, an upscale strip that has drawn residents such a media mogul Barry Diller and David and Victoria Beckham. Glaser and his partner, Jarrett Posner's Posner Group, paid $105 million for the 2.34-acre site last year. It's widely expected to ask more than $300 million.

A sale of the property for that amount would nearly double the Miami-Dade County record, which was set earlier this year by Mark Zuckerberg's deal for a $170 million house on Indian Creek Island.

For Glaser, the move is a bet that South Florida's ultraluxury market will continue its unprecedented winning streak, even as fears of an AI bubble and global economic uncertainty threaten to dampen the spending power of the wealthy.

Glaser says he sees the continued strength of the market as almost guaranteed.

"We've reached the moon," he says. "Now we're going to Mars, or Saturn."

Man about town

"Can I get a margarita with the fancy Patron and a side of orange juice, no salt?" says Glaser.

It's a gray afternoon in mid-November at Coco, the restaurant at the newly completed Vineta Hotel in Palm Beach, near where he lives with his wife, Kim Glaser, and the youngest of his children. The restaurant is so fancy that there's a menu for dogs. A $23 dish called "Vanity Fur" features seared Ora king salmon and steamed farm greens.

The new hotel is evidence, Glaser says, of the type of sustained investment driving the state's boom. "The amount of money that has being invested — we've never seen this," says Glaser.

After lunch, he takes me for a look at some of Palm Beach's most valuable real estate from the water, on his circa-1930s cruising houseboat, Sea Tabby. He points out the homes of tech billionaires, cosmetics tycoons and socialites. Finally, we visit Glaser's personal home, a 16,000-square-foot Mediterranean-style estate that he is listing for $59 million. Glaser frequently buys and sells homes of his own.

In the garage, he keeps a string of classic cars, including a 1971 Mercedes-Benz 280SE and two Ferraris. A Maybach in front is monogrammed with his initials.

How much money has Glaser actually made in the real-estate game? He can't, or won't say.

"I never add my s-t up, ever," he says.

Glaser grew up in a very different South Florida. His working-class Jewish family lived in a rented two-bedroom apartment on the Bay Harbor Islands in Miami. His father was a hair stylist at the Americana, a resort hotel, while his mom stayed home with the children. Glaser was dyslexic and struggled with schoolwork.

Glaser recalls surfing with his friends on South Beach at a time when Miami was the epicenter of the violent cocaine and marijuana trade, and being pulled over by police who suspected they were there to buy drugs. Glaser still considers himself "a hippie." He routinely smokes marijuana and, when I meet him, is wearing a beaded turquoise bracelet.

As a teenager, Glaser was a waiter at the Regency Hotel, where he got a front row view of how the wealthy lived. Once, when his father struck a deal for some hair pieces with the maître d' at the legendary Petite Marmite restaurant in Palm Beach, the family scored a table there. On the way, they passed Mar-a-Lago. Back then, it was best known as the former home of cereal heiress Marjorie Merriweather Post.

"I went, 'whoa!'" Glaser remembers. "I want a house like that."

After high school, Glaser went to work designing fire-protection systems for residential and commercial buildings. Sitting in long meetings with contractors, he became interested in the development business. In 1989, he had saved up enough to buy a $180,000 Key West-style wood-frame house in Coconut Grove. He was soon approached by a location scout for the supermarket Publix. They wanted to film a commercial there and offered him almost $30,000, enough to cover two years of mortgage payments. He was in business.

Glaser keeps a running list of properties he has bought, sold and built. As of mid-November, it was about 200 long. Homes he's built have been purchased by celebrities such as director Michael Bay and wrestler Hulk Hogan. He bought Jeffrey Epstein's house for $18.5 million in 2021, demolished it and sold the land for $25.8 million later that same year.

Covid supercharged the market beyond even Glaser's wildest dreams, as affluent residents of the Northeast migrated south amid a boom in remote work.

Glaser's biggest deal: the renovation of a nearly 29,000-square-foot home on Tarpon Island, a 2-acre private island in Palm Beach, which he sold for $150 million in 2024. Glaser had bought it with partners for $85 million in 2021.

Glaser says he makes his money on the buy, in what he refers to as "legalized insider trading."

By spotting gaps between seller expectations and where the market is headed, he pounces with lightning speed.

That pace consumes him; his wife of 25 years complains that he never misses a work call. "It's like a drug to him," says Kim.

"If I miss a call, it's $5 million," Glaser retorts. "You know how many bags and earrings that buys?"

She rolls her eyes.

If an agent doesn't deliver his offer to a seller fast enough, he has driven over to the house himself: "I knock on the door and say, 'I'm Todd Michael Glaser. I emailed this to your agent, but I want to make sure you get it.'"

Gonzalez says Glaser knows the market so well that he doesn't even need to see a property before he makes an offer.

"His mentality is to tie it up first, and then go see it," Gonzalez says.

At this point, Glaser has bought and sold so many properties that his name has become a liability, he says, with sellers upping the price when they hear he's the buyer. In recent years, he has resorted to buying in partners' names instead.

Glaser is superstitious about his deals. He was unshaven during our meeting, he says, because he has contracts signed that haven't closed yet.

"I won't shave until I close," he says. "So, if it's a six-month closing, I look like a Rabbi."

In his pocket, he keeps his father's mezuza, a small parchment scroll inscribed with Hebrew verses, but he's dabbling in Christian symbols, too. An avid golfer, his golf ball marker features an image of St. Joseph, which he says brings him luck with sales. When he was about to sell Tarpon Island, he says, he dug a hole in the ground and buried a statue of the saint.

The epicenter of the world

In the years since Covid, the Palm Beach and Miami markets have continued to accelerate, propelled by stock market growth and an influx from Silicon Valley. Billionaires like hedge fund titan Ken Griffin, along with tech moguls like Zuckerberg and Google's Larry Page, have gobbled up nine-figure estates.

That demographic won't flinch at a $300 million house in a few years' time, Glaser says. He's continuing to buy more properties, even as the prices have become too rich for other developers. He is in contract to pay $36.5 million for a home in Manalapan, the Palm Beach County community where Larry Ellison lives. For the first time in his career, he says, institutional investors are taking a look at the spec-home market and expressing interest in his deals.

When I ask Glaser what makes him so confident that the market's hot streak will continue, he asks the waitress at Coco for a piece of paper. On it, he sketches out a map of America. He writes "blue" across the country, then "red" on Florida. The rest of the country experiencing a blue wave only makes the sunshine state look more attractive to wealthy Republicans across the county, he says.

Trump has made Palm Beach "the epicenter of the world," Glaser says, though he adds he isn't political and hasn't voted in 10 years. When he attends friends' events at Mar-a-Lago, he doesn't stand and applaud when the President enters. "I'm not going to stand up for anybody, especially that guy."

Agent Dina Goldentayer recalls what Glaser once said to her when she asked if he planned to keep up this pace forever.

"He compared himself to someone who had struck oil," Goldentayer says. "If you had an oil well underneath you, would you just stop drilling?"

"I'm an animal"

Not everyone is a fan of the temperamental Glaser, who concedes that he can be impatient.

"I don't wanna know that Jack and Jill went up the hill before Jack fell down and broke his crown," he quips. "I just wanna know if Jackie is dead."

"As one of his lawyers put it, you have to manage Todd," says Gonzalez.

When Glaser first began building spec homes in Miami Beach, neighbors complained bitterly about him tearing down classic Mediterranean-style homes and replacing them with white-box, contemporary mansions.

"Neighbors were coming to the city commission and saying, 'Our neighborhoods are being transformed into commercial development sites and these new homes are so large and overwhelming,'" says Daniel Ciraldo, former executive director of Miami Design Preservation League.

When Glaser announced plans to tear down Al Capone's onetime Miami Beach house, local preservationists fiercely opposed the demolition of the 1922 Spanish Colonial-style estate. Glaser, who bought the property in partnership with Gonzalez, says the media buzz helped them quickly flip the property, which was demolished by a subsequent owner. "We owned it for a month and made $5 million," Gonzalez says.

Local agents say Glaser's propensity to flip contracts has also irked sellers and brokers. They see Glaser's behavior as manipulating the system: tying up properties by putting them under contract and then making calls to see if he can score a profitable flip.

"He's like P.T. Barnum," says local agent Dana Koch. "He's a promoter."

When Glaser recently nixed a $160 million deal for a Palm Beach oceanfront estate after going public in the press about the contract signing, the seller's agent was unimpressed, Glaser says. Talking publicly about his deal for the property, which had been asking $185 million, let future buyers know that the seller would part with the property for significantly below ask.

Glaser didn't care. "They should have made me sign an NDA," he says. "They know I'm an animal."

Glaser says he sent the agent a YouTube link to the Kenny Rogers tune "The Gambler," which features the lyric: "You got to know when to hold 'em, Know when to fold 'em."

data.title: UK auto production rises 4.8% from a year ago in October, SMMT data shows
data.description:
British vehicle production grew 4.8% year-on-year in October, propelled by a recovery in car manufacturing after a major cyber incident last year halted production at Jaguar Land Rover, the country's largest automaker, industry data showed on Friday.

  • Total vehicle production grew to 64,141 units in October, the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT) said

data.title: Cautious consumers gear up for Black Friday as inflation woes bite
data.description:
Key points:
  • Consumers seen spending despite cost-of-living gloom
  • Target, Kohl's, rivals point to belt-tightening
  • Toy prices surge on supply chain woes, including plastics
  • AI looms as wild card

By Nicholas P. Brown, Juveria Tabassum and Danielle Kaye

Neither high fuel prices nor stubborn inflation are expected to stop US shoppers from spending robustly as their turkey hangovers wear off on Black Friday. But below healthy top-line forecasts lie signs of stress.

Holiday spending — which unofficially begins on Black Friday — is seen topping last year's strong figures by 4%-6%, several economic forecasts show. But most of the gains will be attributable to inflation which, at 3.8%, is about a percentage point higher than in each of the last two years.

The National Retail Federation sees November-December holiday retail sales rising 4.2% year-over-year, to just above $1 trillion. The Mastercard Economics Institute and EY Parthenon each forecast sales to rise more than 5%.

Eventual final results often beat pre-holiday estimates. Still, consumer sentiment remains shaky. This month, voters punished US President Donald Trump for an Iran War that's pushed the cost of living higher, handing Democrats sweeping electoral victories.

A November survey by the National Retail Federation found that 82% of consumers are taking steps to manage holiday costs, like buying less expensive gifts.

Los Angeles resident Felicia Cox, 50, said that while her holiday spending will be roughly stable, inflation is impacting how she thinks. "I want to get more gifts that people will actually use or need," said Cox, a sales representative, while browsing in an L.A. Marshalls last week. "I feel like people aren't able to afford as much stuff."

Worries aside, some 87% of 1,200 consumers surveyed by Deloitte in October planned to participate in the five-day shopping period from Thanksgiving through "Cyber Monday," November 30 — the highest in a decade, according to Deloitte.

"People like to spend during the holidays," even when there's a "persisting undercurrent of stress,” said Katie Thomas, who leads the Kearney Consumer Institute, part of global consulting firm Kearney.

Middle- and lower-income shoppers — who have been trading down for months — were however more likely than wealthy ones to spend less, according to the Kearney survey.

Target , Dollar Tree and Kohl's have all pointed to belt-tightening during recent earnings calls. Kohl's CEO Michael Bender on Tuesday cited an "increasingly choiceful" consumer that is "looking to stretch every dollar."

Holiday spending forecasts mostly predated the recent stock market correction that followed the midterms, turmoil at chipmaker Nvidia , and mounting concerns around an AI bubble. The decline could dampen the wealth effect that has seen affluent shoppers splurge on gadgets and accessories, UBS analysts said in a note on Tuesday.

TOYS TAKE A HIT

Higher input costs, particularly from petrol derivatives like plastic, are hitting some products more than others.

Prices of toys — generally high in plastic — have risen 13.2% since the start of the year, pushing Barbie maker Mattel this month to cut its annual forecast as consumers balked at higher costs.

Some unlikely products are buoying the toy category. Best Buy and Target have both flagged trading cards — including Pokemon and Magic: The Gathering products — as a key growth driver. Squishy NeeDoh toys were selling for $24.99 on Amazon in October, nearly triple the price a year earlier on hot demand, according to e-commerce marketing platform Omnisend.

Toy maker Learning Resources Inc — a plaintiff in lawsuits that overturned Trump's tariffs — is seeing demand roughly flat, said CEO Rick Woldenberg, though he added it's hard to predict demand before Black Friday.

"People can't shop until they have their turkey," Woldenberg said.

AI could also scramble the year's shopping dynamics. As shoppers use AI to find bargains or even complete purchases — and retailers become increasingly adept at altering price quickly through AI — the deepest discounts could come closer to Christmas, as consumers and retailers both wait out the market, said Ryan Orabone, a consultant at Spaulding Ridge.

"My advice to shoppers is to be patient," he said. "Don't jump on the first deal you see."

data.title: HEG, formerly known as HEG Graphite set to list today - All you need to know
data.description:
HEG Ltd., formerly known as HEG Graphite Ltd. following its corporate restructuring, is set to list on the bourses on Friday, November 27, marking the final milestone of a composite scheme of arrangement designed to unlock shareholder value.

Under the NCLT-approved restructuring, effective September 1, 2026, the original listed entity was renamed HEG Advanced Materials Ltd. to house its green power, battery energy storage solutions, and advanced materials businesses, while its core graphite electrode operations were demerged into the newly listed HEG Ltd.

For investors who held the undivided stock on September 4, 2026, the final trading session before the September 7 ex-demerger record date, when shares closed near ₹728, the corporate action delivered a 1:1 share entitlement.

Eligible shareholders retained their existing equity shares in HEG Advanced Materials Ltd., which is currently trading around ₹283 per share, and automatically received one fully paid-up equity share of ₹2 face value in the newly carved-out HEG Ltd. for every share held.

Additionally, the composite scheme merged Bhilwara Energy Ltd. into HEG Advanced Materials at an 8:7 share exchange ratio, separating mature cash-generating graphite operations from capital-intensive clean-energy investments.

The timing of the pure-play graphite listing coincides with clear signs of a cyclical bottoming out, as echoed by company management. Global industry dynamics have tightened considerably following GrafTech’s announcement of an additional 51,000-tonne (51kt) capacity cut in Mexico, reducing its total capacity to roughly 127kt, alongside two consecutive rounds of price hikes implemented in March 2026 and September 2026.

On the demand front, an estimated 62 million tonnes (mt) of global Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) steel capacity additions between 2026 and 2028 is projected to generate incremental demand support of 90kt to 100kt for graphite electrodes, according to an Aditya Birla Capital research note.

Backed by tighter supply and rising steelmaker demand, Aditya Birla Capital expects graphite electrode producers to push through a near-term price hike of approximately $1,000 per tonne during the upcoming round of contract negotiations.

This pricing recovery is projected to drive a sharp earnings rebound for HEG Ltd., with Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA), anticipated to expand from ₹390 crore in financial year 2026, and a current implied annualized run-rate of ~₹740 crore to between ₹1,100 crore and ₹1,250 crore by financial year 2028 and 2029.

data.title: Tokyo Inflation Accelerated, Keeping BOJ Rate Hike in Play
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Consumer inflation in Japan's capital picked up in November, reinforcing market expectations that the Bank of Japan will raise interest rates again next month.

Core consumer inflation in the Tokyo metropolitan area, which excludes volatile fresh food prices, climbed 2.9% in November from a year earlier, compared with October's 2.6% rise, government data showed Friday.

That was roughly in line with the 3.0% increase expected in a poll of economists by data provider Quick. The Tokyo figures are closely watched as a leading indicator of nationwide price trends.

The firmer reading strengthens the case for the BOJ to further tighten monetary policy at its final meeting of the year on Dec. 17-18. The central bank raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September and stated last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target.

The BOJ has said that consumer prices face upward pressure from higher crude oil costs amid Middle East tensions, a weak yen and rising prices for electronics components tied to artificial-intelligence demand.

BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda warned in Parliament last week that core consumer inflation is likely to climb well above 2%, reiterating the bank's readiness to raise interest rates further.

On Thursday, hawkish BOJ policy board member Naoki Tamura also urged the central bank to bring the policy rate toward a neutral level soon and act swiftly if upside price risks build. He said it is possible to assess financial conditions within a few months of each rate hike.

Write to Megumi Fujikawa at megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com
